chunk_findings.detail: `cut_notice` always tells the caller to "see the rest with --all", but that flag only raises the limit to `LIST_MAX_LIMIT`, which is already the limit whenever the list is truncated after `--all` or for a phase list (`_UNPAGED` / `_limit`). Given `task list --all` (or `phase list`) whose engine result is `{truncated: true, shown: LIST_MAX_LIMIT, total: LIST_MAX_LIMIT+1, ...}`, the footer still recommends `--all`. Repeating it returns the same page, so a row past the cap (P-schedule, oldest-touched) is still absent and the miss looks like "no such phase".
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/viewers_lists.py:cut_notice

chunk_findings.detail: CLI `phase` lists now default to `LIST_MAX_LIMIT`, but the tool path still does `int(a.get("limit") or 25)` unless `all` is set. A tool call `{kind: "phase"}` (no `limit`, no `all`) therefore still returns 25 of 199, newest-first, so P-schedule stays off the payload. The same call on the CLI returns up to the max. The new `all` branch does not implement the unpaged phase default this change added on the command surface.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_all_lifts_the_page_size_for_every_kind_and_phase_is_unpaged` never lists phases. It only checks `VL._limit` returns `LIST_MAX_LIMIT` for kind `"phase"`. The bug is a service/CLI slice: `phase list` printed 50 of 199 and a phase past page one vanished. A build that still slices phase rows at 50 (or ignores `_limit`) satisfies this test, so the regression can close Bd515797884 without failing on that input. The match test has the same hole: tasks are newest-first and `T-needle` is added last, so `view_list(..., match="needle", limit=1)` still returns it if match runs after the page cut.

Unfixed `phase list` pages at 50, and 5 is under that cap, so stdout contains every phase and no truncation footer; the test passes and can close Bd515797884 without ever seeing “50 of 199”. chunk_findings.detail: The new test requires `phase list` to emit P0–P4 with no `PARTIAL` after `R.LIST_DEFAULT_LIMIT` is set to 2, and it still demands a cut `task list`. Nothing in this change alters list limits or phase paging: `view_list` only gains a noqa, and `cut_notice` only rewords a footer. The `many` fixture already sets `V.DEFAULT_LIMIT` to 3 (the constant this file’s other tests actually page on) and adds eight tasks. Under that, `phase list` of five phases is still a page of three, so `PARTIAL` is in stdout and `all(f"P{i} " in out …) and "PARTIAL" not in out` fails. If phase list instead ignores both patches and keeps the documented page of 50, five phases all print with no `PARTIAL` on unfixed code, so the assertion does not fail the bug (199 phases, page 50, `--all` still truncated). Either way the regression does not lock the fix, and the bug’s paging/`--all` behavior is unchanged.
